DESCRIPTION.STACK_TEXT: Stacks are LIFO (Last-In First-Out) data structures, where the last element inserted will be the first one to be removed. Thus, a stack allows access to only one data item - the last one inserted. To process the second-to-last item inserted, the last one must be removed.

DESCRIPTION.TITLE: QUEUE DESCRIPTION
DESCRIPTION.TEXT: A Queue is a dynamic data structure that allows for the removal and insertion of new elements. A queue is subject to the following operating rule: whenever a removal occurs, the element removed is the one that has been in the structure the longest. In other words, the first object inserted into the queue is also the first to be removed, also known by the acronym FIFO (First-In-First-Out).
